items.headline: Council closed-session agenda listed two lawsuits against Cupertino, including one by YIMBY
items.summary: The November 17 City Council agenda listed a closed-session conference with legal counsel on existing litigation: Lixin (Leon) Chen, et al. v. City of Cupertino (Case No. 25CA462857) and Yes in My Backyard, et al. v. City of Cupertino (Case No. 25CA263924), both in Santa Clara County Superior Court. The agenda gives only the case names and numbers.

items.headline: Council agenda included ordinance changing City Council compensation
items.summary: The November 17 agenda listed consideration of an ordinance amending Cupertino Municipal Code Section 2.16.020 on City Council compensation. The agenda excerpt does not give the proposed amounts.

items.headline: Council agenda listed community funding and festival fee waiver recommendations
items.summary: The November 17 agenda listed council subcommittee recommendations on the city's Community Funding Policy and on festival fee waivers. The same agenda also included amendments to the Council Procedures Manual, an item postponed from May 5, 2026.

items.headline: Campbell commission agenda: rezone 480 Chapman from commercial to single-family
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed a public hearing on a request from the owners of 480 Chapman, a single-family house on a neighborhood-commercial lot, to change it to Low Density Residential and R-1-10 zoning and drop its T4N.M-O form-based designation. The stated aim is to end the house's legal nonconforming status. The commission was asked to recommend approval to the City Council, tentatively set for December 1, 2026.

items.headline: Eden Housing's 251-unit project on N. Wolfe Road up for approval
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed Architectural and Site Approval and Tree Removal Permits for a 251-unit residential development at 10333 N. Wolfe Road, applicant Eden Housing. The plan includes trail improvements and the removal and replacement of 117 protected trees.

items.headline: Eight-story, 200-unit rental building proposed at 720 San Antonio Road
items.summary: The November 9 City Council agenda listed a prescreening request to rezone 720 San Antonio Road, a roughly 1.35-acre site, from Service Commercial to Planned Community/Planned Home zoning. The change would allow 200 rental units in an eight-story structure. Prescreening gives the applicant council feedback before a formal application.

items.headline: Preschool for up to 192 kids proposed at 855 E. Homestead
items.summary: The November 9 Planning Commission agenda listed a Special Development Permit to demolish a vacant commercial building on a 1.11-acre site. In its place would go a 16,000-square-foot, two-story Primrose Schools childcare and preschool for up to 192 children, with a new eight-foot concrete block wall along the western and part of the southern property lines.

items.headline: Sunnyvale planned rewrite of citywide residential parking rules
items.summary: The November 9 Planning Commission agenda listed a recommendation to the City Council on an ordinance that would repeal and replace the zoning code's parking chapter (19.46) to revise residential off-street parking requirements. It would also amend the Downtown, Lawrence Station, and El Camino Real specific plan chapters, the definitions chapter, and the Dual Urban Opportunity Housing chapter.
